items.prompt: White to move. The black pawn on c5 attacks d4, and the pawn on d4 holds up e5. Find the pawn move that gives d4 a pawn defender.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is c3 (depth 16).
Before the move one white piece defends d4 (the queen).
After c3 two white pieces defend d4 (pawn and queen).
dxc5 is at least 0.25 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: How many pieces defend d4 now, and how many attack it?
Which pawn can stand next to d4 and guard it?
The c-pawn moves one square.
items.explain: The pawn on c3 defends d4, so the queen is no longer the only defender, and after a trade on d4 a pawn can retake and rebuild the chain. It is the engine's first choice at depth 16. Capturing on c5 gives up the base and is at least 0.25 pawns worse.

feedback_by_move.d4c5: dxc5 gives up the base of the chain. At depth 16 it is at least 0.25 pawns worse than c3.

items.prompt: White to move. The knight on b1 wants to reach c2, where it will defend d4 from behind. Which knight move keeps the bishop on c1 free to use the diagonal toward h6 and still heads for c2?

claims.statement: After Na3 the bishop on c1 can move to five squares.
After Nbd2 the bishop on c1 can move to no square.
A knight on a3 attacks c2.
A knight on d2 does not attack c2.

hints: Count the squares the bishop on c1 could reach after each knight move, and ask which square each knight can go to next.
Which knight move puts a piece on the bishop's own diagonal?
The knight on d2 would stand in front of the bishop and cannot reach c2.
items.explain: The knight on d2 blocks the bishop on c1 completely and cannot reach c2 from there. The knight on a3 stays off the bishop's diagonal and reaches c2 next.

items.prompt: Black to move. The pawn on c5 and the knight on c6 attack d4; the knight on f3 and the queen defend it (White has not played c3). Suppose Black plays the knight from e7 to f5. Will Black then have more attackers on d4 than White has defenders? Count first.

claims.statement: After Nf5 three black pieces attack d4 (pawn c5, knights c6 and f5).
Two white pieces defend d4 (knight f3 and queen d1).

hints: List the black pieces that attack d4 now, then add the knight.
From f5 a knight attacks d4, e3, g3, h4, d6, e7, g7 and h6.
Three attackers against two defenders.
items.explain: Two black pieces attack d4 now. The knight on f5 would add a third, so the count would be three against two. White has no pawn on c3 to help, so White must add a defender or give up something; this is why the pawn move to c3 comes first in the main line.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's pawn on c5 and knight on c6 attack d4, and the knights on d7 and c6 attack e5. Find a bishop move that adds a third defender to d4.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is Be3 (depth 16).
Before the move two white pieces defend d4 (knight f3 and queen).
After Be3 three white pieces defend d4.
dxc5 is at least 0.35 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
Qd2 is at least 0.6 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders of d4.
Which bishop move defends d4 and brings a piece out?
The bishop on c1 can reach e3.
items.explain: Be3 adds a defender: the bishop, the knight and the queen guard d4 against two attackers, and it is the engine's first choice at depth 16. Qd2 leaves two defenders against two attackers and is at least 0.6 pawns worse.

feedback_by_move.d4c5: dxc5 gives up the base of the chain: at least 0.35 pawns worse at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.d1d2: Qd2 does not add a defender that the bishop on c1 can then use: the count on d4 stays two against two, and the engine rates it at least 0.6 pawns worse (depth 16).

items.prompt: White to move. Black has just played ...a6. White's knight on c3 could jump to b5, where it eyes d6 and c7. Does the jump work, or does it lose material? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: A black pawn attacks b5.
The knight on c3 attacks b5.
Nb5 is at least 3 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which black pawn guards b5 after ...a6?
What happens to a knight that lands on a square a pawn attacks?
The pawn on a6 takes the knight.
items.explain: After ...a6 the pawn attacks b5, so the knight that jumps there is captured by a pawn and White gets only a pawn back. The engine rates Nb5 at least 3 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16). That is what ...a6 prepares: it takes b5 from White's pieces, and later ...b5 gains space [I].

items.prompt: Black to move. What do you play?

claims.statement: ...c5, ...Be7 and ...h6 are within 0.4 pawns of each other (depth 16).
...a5 is at least 0.4 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
...Nc6 is at least 0.4 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
...f6 is at least 0.6 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which pawn lever hits the base d4?
The base has not been attacked yet.
One pawn move is the engine's first choice.
items.explain: The lever against d4 is the engine's first choice at depth 16, and developing the bishop (or a waiting move such as ...h6) is close. Quiet moves on the wing and the immediate knight move are at least 0.4 pawns worse, and ...f6 at least 0.6.

feedback_by_move.a7a5: ...a5 does nothing about d4 and e5: at least 0.4 pawns worse at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.b8c6: ...Nc6 attacks e5 and d4 at once, but with the c-pawn still on c7 the base is not yet under pressure; at least 0.4 pawns worse at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.f7f6: ...f6 hits the head before pieces stand behind it: at least 0.6 pawns worse at depth 16.

dxc5 is at least 0.2 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders of d4.
A pawn attacks d4, and a second attacker will come.
A knight move to the kingside defends both d4 and e5.
items.explain: A piece developed to a square that guards d4 is the engine's choice at depth 16. Capturing on c5 gives up the base and is a little less accurate (at least 0.2 pawns worse, about 0.25 to 0.35 in our tests); Qd2 is at least 0.6 pawns worse.

feedback_by_move.d4c5: dxc5 gives up the base of the chain: a little less accurate, at least 0.2 pawns worse at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.d1d2: Qd2 develops without adding a defender to d4: at least 0.6 pawns worse at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. What do you play?

claims.statement: Nf3, Be2, g3, h3 and a3 are within 0.4 pawns of each other (depth 16).
After Nf3 three white pieces defend d4.

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders of d4 now.
A knight move to the kingside adds a defender of d4 and of e5.
Knight to f3.
items.explain: Nf3 gives d4 a third defender and e5 a second, and it is the engine's first choice at depth 16. Be2, g3, h3 and a3 are also within 0.4 pawns, but only Nf3 adds a defender to the key pawn, which is the idea of this lesson.
